title: Aside vs Google Chrome: Is a Chrome Alternative Worth It?
summary: Already have Gemini in Chrome? See if a Chrome alternative is worth it: real tests of Chrome auto browse and Aside, a ten-row comparison and what each costs.
body_markdown:
On January 30, 2026, a[WIRED reviewer asked Chrome's auto browse](https://www.wired.com/story/google-chrome-auto-browse-hands-on/) for two symphony seats next to an aisle. It picked $185 seats in separate rows, and he bought two together himself. Auto browse is part of Gemini in Chrome, which answers questions about your tabs. With a paid Google AI plan, auto browse does multi-step tasks on websites.


Aside is a browser with an AI agent built in. It works on the sites you're signed in to and in the apps on your computer, where it[ranked #1 in a benchmark run by Scale](https://aside.com/blog/aside-computer-use-ranks-number-one-in-cua-driver-bench) . The agent is available in free plans.


So is a Chrome alternative worth it? Stay with Chrome and Gemini if your tasks stay on websites and you already pay for a Google AI plan. Switch to Aside if you want to run complex tasks that extend beyond the browser into your desktop apps.


Aside and Chrome with Gemini compared: what the AI does, desktop apps, the free plan, using your own AI plan, AI models, scheduled tasks, permissions, sign-ins, memory and working from your phone.


## How do you use Gemini in Chrome, and how do you start a task in Aside?#


In Chrome, you click Ask Gemini, describe the task, press Submit, review the plan and press Start Task. In Aside, you open a new tab, switch the box from Search to Ask, and type the task in a plain sentence. The agent works in your own browser, on sites you're already signed in to.


To ask about a page instead, click Ask Gemini in Chrome. The current tab is shared by default, and on a computer you can share up to 10 open tabs or type @ to add one. In Aside, press Cmd/Ctrl+E or click Ask Aside in the toolbar, and the side panel opens with that page attached.


While a Chrome task runs you can press Take over task, Resume or Stop. Aside's[guide to your first tasks](https://aside.com/blog/how-to-use-aside) uses prompts like this one:


> Find a shelf under $80 on Amazon that can be delivered to our office by tomorrow. And add the best one to my cart. Don't check it out.


## Does Chrome auto browse finish a real errand on its own?#


In two reviews from early 2026, it found the sites, reached checkout and stopped before the final order. Both reviewers also changed what it picked: the seats in one test, the bread in the other. ZDNET's Elyse Betters Picaro wrote on February 18, 2026: "Auto Browse is not a trigger-and-forget AI tool."


WIRED published[a hands-on with auto browse](https://www.wired.com/story/google-chrome-auto-browse-hands-on/) on January 30, 2026, run on Google's $20 a month tier. The first prompt:


> I want to book two tickets to the SF symphony tonight. I don't want to pay for orchestra seating, but the tickets don't need to be the cheapest ones available. Please pick the two seats next to an aisle.


Auto browse found the right site and performance and logged each step. After a couple of minutes it stopped and notified the reviewer to press Order Now. It had picked $185 side-box seats by an aisle, in separate rows. He took over and bought two cheaper seats next to each other.


A later prompt asked for research:


> I'm looking for some two-person tent camping spots that are available to book in April or May. Looking to stay four nights, hopefully over the weekend. The campground must be within a three hour drive of San Francisco. Give me five solid options, with reasons for picking each.


That run took almost 15 minutes. It checked availability at one campground, Point Reyes, and told him to check the Reserve California website for the rest. WIRED still wrote that its multistep ability "was noticeably better than similar agent tools that I tested last year".


In[ZDNET's test](https://www.zdnet.com/article/chrome-auto-browse/) , Betters Picaro had items in a Walmart cart and asked Gemini to check out. It asked permission to sign in with Google Password Manager, loaded the cart, went through checkout and stopped at the final review page. She stopped the task to ask for sourdough bread, and it added ACE Bakery Sourdough, not the brand she buys. She found you can't add a follow-up mid-task. You stop and send a new prompt, or take over.


She also asked it to email her husband Corey about ordering groceries for a Friday party. It asked to connect Gmail, picked the right Corey, drafted the message and waited for her to send it. She reported that in February 2026 Google AI Pro allowed up to 20 multi-step tasks a day and Ultra up to 200, and she hit the Pro limit while writing.


## Can Aside finish a real task from one sentence?#


In one independent audit it did, after one sign-in. Michael Wilson audited Aside on Windows on October 6-7, 2026, using a free account. He asked in one sentence for a Google Sheet comparing Figma, Framer and Webflow pricing. He wrote: "Twelve minutes later I had a cited, four-tab Sheet in my own Google account."


[Wilson's audit](https://michaelawilson.co/aside-ux-audit) records the task timer at 12m 16s. A Sources tab in the Sheet lets you check each price. One pricing page carried instructions addressed to AI readers, and the agent declined them. He called the result "a pretty good job for one shot."


Google Sheets was signed out mid-task even though he had imported his Chrome cookies. The agent asked him to sign in, and he answered 1 minute 23 seconds later. If a task needs an account, sign in before you start it.


The task used about 145 of the month's 500 free credits, or 29%, and the result did not show the cost. Wilson estimated the free plan covers about three tasks like his a month. If you would run more, the Free plan includes "Bring your own subscription": sign in with Claude Pro or Max, or with ChatGPT Plus or Pro through Codex. If you use Claude through its Chrome extension today, see[Aside vs Claude in Chrome](https://aside.com/blog/aside-vs-claude-in-chrome) .


## Is Aside a good Chrome alternative?#


Two people wrote on X in November 2026 that they use it in place of Chrome.[Aditya R Sharma's post](https://x.com/adityaarsharma/status/2123085430799347982) from November 18, 2026 opens: "Finally replaced my Chrome browser." He wrote that he switched "because I wanted my browser to actually get work done." Others posted jobs they hand to Aside, such as travel bookings and weekly cross-posting.


Aditya R Sharma on X, Nov 18, 2026


Anson Lin[wrote](https://x.com/ansonlin/status/2119201021037547698) on November 7, 2026: "i rarely even touch google chrome/claude anymore" and "i run everything on aside".


Anson Lin on X, Nov 7, 2026


Erik Gao compared four browsers on November 19, 2026 in a post that begins "AI browser test: Chrome vs. Aside vs. Facet vs. Dia." He opened one company's site in each and asked, "What font is this page using?" His result in[that one test](https://x.com/gaaoyi/status/2123648680150610168) : "Only Aside answered." In a reply he wrote, "Chrome and Dia do not reach for CSS." We cover[how Aside and Dia differ](https://aside.com/blog/aside-vs-dia) in a separate post.


Arsh[wrote about sign-ins](https://x.com/be_arsh/status/2120323210470211886) on November 10, 2026: "zero auth problems, all my existing cookies and logins just work natively with no weird session re auth".


Jason Wang pairs Aside with Muse, a separate personal-assistant product, and[books travel with the two](https://x.com/jwang815/status/2122406605891448963) . On November 16, 2026 he wrote: "I pretty much make all of my travel bookings with Muse + Aside Browser combo. Nothing gets blocked."


Rahul Singh Bhadoriya[cross-posts his design work](https://x.com/rahulbhadoriiya/status/2123268758907314635) . Milan Stankovic had[a setting he and his lead dev couldn't find](https://x.com/milstan/status/2120023917314379795) . On November 9, 2026 he wrote: "Both my lead dev and I couldn't find an option we needed in the UI of a cloud provider (which shall remain unnamed). I gave it to Claude plus @AsideAI browser. Done."


Mikdaam connected his own Claude Code plan and listed[two uses](https://x.com/bmikdaam/status/2122729664313720927) on November 17, 2026. One is a prompt: "doomscroll around 100-150 posts for me and make me a summary of my for you feed". The other is "prepare my travel to Toronto, next week".


## Can Aside or Chrome work in your desktop apps?#


In Aside, yes, once you turn on Computer Use. It is off by default and available on every plan, on Mac and Windows. Aside announced it on November 6, 2026. Nothing on Google's Chrome auto browse help page documents controlling desktop apps such as Keynote. Google's launch demo filled in a form with information from a PDF.


The guide's example prompt for it:


> Take the numbers in this Google Sheet and build a chart slide in Keynote.


You turn Computer Use on under Settings > Agents, then type @ in the prompt to pick the app. On a Mac, Computer Use needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permission. On Windows, clicking and typing take over your mouse and keyboard until that step ends.


Screenshot: the Computer Use toggle in Aside under Settings > Agents.


Our walkthrough of[five Computer Use tasks on Mac and iPhone](https://aside.com/blog/how-to-use-aside-computer-use) shows the prompt Adeline Kim from our team typed for each, from finding a dinner spot in an iPhone app to editing a video in DaVinci Resolve. Aside has also published its[Cua Driver Bench results for Computer Use](https://aside.com/blog/aside-computer-use-ranks-number-one-in-cua-driver-bench) .


## Can you schedule a task without leaving the browser?#


In Aside, yes. A routine is a set of instructions plus a schedule, and each run starts a new task. Routines run while your computer is awake and Aside is open. Google's schedules are set up in the Gemini app. In Chrome, a saved Skill reruns a prompt when you type / on another page.


You set up a routine under Settings > Routines, or ask for one in chat. In the Gemini app, you click Task and describe what and when. Google's example: "Every day at 7 AM, look through my emails, calendar, and Drive, and let me know what to prioritize for the day." Pro and Ultra tasks can run hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, up to 50 active schedules. With Plus or no subscription, a task runs up to once a day in a general window, up to 10 schedules. Run times are approximate.


A Gemini task that uses your local Chrome also needs the device and Chrome running. Gemini's remote browser keeps working with the device off, but Google's help page says: "For certain steps, like signing in to a website, the task pauses until you take over".


On November 24, 2026 we gave Aside this prompt once, as a normal task:


> Find three things people in software are discussing today. Link to the original source for each and give me one question I could answer from experience. Don't write or publish a post.


It returned three items, each dated and linked to its original source, with a question for each:


1. Farid Zakaria's November 23 write-up on TryNix running Firefox inside a Firefox tab. "What's a tool you'd try in a browser tab but wouldn't bother installing?"
2. Quad9's November 24 notice that it will stop answering DNS queries from France. "When a service you depended on went away, what made it harder to replace than you expected?"
3. Anthropic's November 23 beta announcement about misuse monitoring without keeping customer logs. "What's one thing you won't hand to an AI tool at work because you don't know who can see the logs?"


Example: Aside's routine form filled in with that prompt, named Morning LinkedIn research and set to Daily at 9:00 AM. The form is in our own account and was not saved.


We interviewed an Aside user on November 24, 2026. A colleague pitched Aside to him as a Chrome replacement, and he said "it replaced Chrome for me like pretty quickly". He has no time to post on LinkedIn every day on top of his job, and he found ghostwriters cost "at minimum, like $2,000 a month". Instead, a routine runs a research report every morning on trending news and post formats. He also had Aside create a calendar block where he talks through his unfiltered ideas, and Aside turns them into a post for his audience. Nothing posts automatically.


## What does each AI ask before it pays, sends or signs in?#


Aside has a Final confirm toggle in the task box. With it on, the agent waits before it pays, posts, sends, deletes or submits. It is off by default, so turn it on for tasks that touch money or other people. Google's help page says: "You're responsible for Gemini's actions during a task, including mistakes and unexpected results like purchases."


Wilson tried Final confirm both ways. With it off, he asked the agent to email his own address. It wrote "I'm sending this now as requested" and sent it. With it on, the same request stopped at a card showing the full email, with Cancel and Confirm buttons.


Every Aside task also has a permission mode: Read only, Guard or Full access. Guard is the default and keeps the agent to folders you approve.


Google's help page says Gemini in Chrome "aims to ask for your review and confirmation before certain actions", including "Sending communications" and "Submitting web forms", and may ask you to take over for "Finalizing financial transactions". The same page says its safeguards "do not guarantee protection against all risks". Its list of possible mistakes includes "Completing a purchase or ordering something without your permission".


For sign-ins, Google says: "Google doesn't share your passwords with Gemini in Chrome or other sites." Aside's Vault is a built-in password manager on the Free plan. It fills the sign-in form so[the agent never receives the password](https://aside.com/blog/ai-agent-that-doesnt-get-blocked) . You set the access policy for AI agents under Settings > Passwords.


## What does it take to switch from Chrome to Aside?#


An import from Chrome. Each Chrome profile imports into its own Aside profile. It supports bookmarks, history, passwords, cookies, open tabs, tab groups and extensions, and the importer reports its results for each type. Aside runs on macOS 15 or later, and on Windows 10 version 22H2 or later or Windows 11.


Setup took 4:11 in Wilson's run. Of that, 69 seconds was the Chrome import waiting for Chrome to close completely, so quit Chrome before you import.


## Is the AI agent free in Chrome and in Aside?#


Aside's Free plan includes the agent, 500 credits a month and 3 active routines. For Chrome auto browse, Google's help page for computers lists 18 or over, in the US, an English device language, the latest Chrome, Safe Browsing on Standard or Enhanced, and a personal Google account on Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra. The rollout is gradual.


Aside Pro is $20 a month, with unlimited routines and 3 times the Free usage. Max is $200 a month. The[pricing page](https://aside.com/pricing) has the full plans.


### FAQ#


**Does either one work on a phone?**


Chrome auto browse does on Android. Google's Android help page says it works in Chrome on Android for people 18 or over "in the US or India" on Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra, and that after you start a task "you don't need to stay in the Chrome app". The same page says it is "not available in Live chats or Gemini in Chrome on iPhone or iPad". Aside runs on Mac and Windows only and has no iPhone app. On Pro and Max, Channels let you message Aside from Slack, Discord or Telegram while your computer is on and Aside is running.


**What is the best Chrome alternative with an AI agent?**


Aside's Free plan includes the agent. Our roundup of the[best AI browsers](https://aside.com/blog/best-ai-browsers) compares eight, including Chrome with Gemini.


**Can Chrome AI run on my Claude or ChatGPT plan?**


By Chrome AI, people mean Gemini in Chrome. Google's help page says you can "Switch between Gemini models", and it documents no option to use another provider's plan. Aside's Free plan lets you sign in with a Claude or ChatGPT plan you already pay for.


**Does Aside remember what I tell it?**


Yes. Aside saves memories from chats and tasks as Markdown files on your computer. You can edit them under Settings > Memory. Context Awareness, which summarizes what you browse, is off until you turn it on.


The quickest way to see if switching is worth it is to run one of your own tasks on the Free plan. For a longer routine, see how one[replies to Instagram comments with a link](https://aside.com/blog/free-manychat-alternative-instagram-comment-link) . Then[download Aside](https://aside.com/download) .
